decisions.reason: Uses agent-session-log.txt and env-state.txt to tie the pwsh tool worker and web session to the host process loaded from the npm global tree being replaced; explains the GUI death at the link phase, the worker dying with the host, and quotes the log's unknown final tool outcome. Frames it as a structural self-host hazard, not a network failure, without any universal every-platform claim.

Explains env-state.txt accurately: package content present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale, so PATH resolution fails before content matters and content presence does not prove a complete install. Links the hand-swapped nonstandard tree to the missing shims and explicitly rejects hand-swapping directories or hand-making shims in favor of a formal npm install.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: rerun npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 from an external CLI/terminal outside the stopped host so npm regenerates all three shims, verify dsh --version equals rc.1, align the source-reference checkout to dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1 without unrelated edits. Clearly separates the recorded repair and user-left verification from anything the candidate performed.

States the agent must recognize it runs inside the upgrade target and must never execute the global install itself, only hand off an external procedure: stop the host first, then exact-version pinned install from a shell not spawned by dsh, then restart the host, hard-refresh the browser, and verify. Distinguishes stop-host-first and exact pinning as known upgrade discipline from the additional self-host no-execute rule.

Describes a pre-execution guard that matches global npm installs targeting dsh against the session's own runtime/module path (process.execPath vs npm prefix) and emits the handoff procedure. Uses the alpha.5-to-rc.1 version-only 252-file diff to skip plugin re-migration, checks shims/version markers and actual plugin loading after restart/refresh, and defers dsh-old-* backup cleanup until rc.1 is confirmed — all specific to the supplied tags, no code changes.

caps.reason: Final protocol is categorically to refuse executing the global install from inside the target host and hand the external procedure to the user; no affirmative advice to run or retry it in-session.
The report explicitly rejects directory swaps, hand-made shims, --no-bin-links, and copying over the old tree; the final fix is the formal external pinned npm install.
